commits.message:
fix(security): close /docs Web Cache Deception gap

Remove /docs, /redoc, /openapi.json from EXEMPTED_PATH_PATTERNS in SecurityHeadersMiddleware. These three paths are auth-protected by DocsAuthMiddleware (mcpgateway/main.py:2423), so exempting them from the no-store/private cache policy let a shared cache (CDN, reverse proxy) replay an authenticated docs/schema response to unauthenticated viewers — the canonical Web Cache Deception pattern.

Also tighten the per-server well-known regex from /servers/.*/... to /servers/[^/]+/... to match the actual single-segment {server_id} route shape (see mcpgateway/routers/server_well_known.py:73).

The fail-secure default in _is_protected_path() ensures these paths now inherit no-store/private/Pragma/Expires/Vary: Authorization headers without an explicit pattern entry.

Signed-off-by: Jonathan Springer <jps@s390x.com>
commits.author: Jonathan Springer

commits.message:
test: drop autouse admin-api fixture from unit conftest

Revert the session-scoped autouse enable_admin_api_for_tests fixture in tests/unit/mcpgateway/conftest.py. It is unrelated to the cache-control hardening goal (the new tests live under tests/security/) and contradicts the existing test design at tests/conftest.py:75-89, which deliberately keeps MCPGATEWAY_ADMIN_API_ENABLED=false to keep import mcpgateway.main cheap.

Tests that need admin routes mounted should opt into the existing main_app_with_admin_api fixture (tests/conftest.py:350) rather than rely on a global mutation that cannot be reliably reversed (FastAPI does not support reliable route un-mounting).

Signed-off-by: Jonathan Springer <jps@s390x.com>
commits.author: Jonathan Springer

commits.message:
test(security): tighten cache-hardening assertions

Fix five test-quality bugs in tests/security/test_security_headers.py:

- test_cache_headers_on_error_responses had no assertion at all; now asserts no-store, private, Pragma, and Expires on a 404 response.
- test_cache_headers_on_nested_endpoints used 'or' between no-store and private; the contract is both. Switch to two separate asserts.
- test_security_headers_disabled only asserted status_code == 200; now verifies that X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, X-XSS-Protection, CSP, and Referrer-Policy are all absent.
- test_x_frame_options_empty_string used a short-circuit 'or' so it always passed; now asserts header absence outright.
- test_exempted_endpoints_can_be_cached passed when only one of no-store/private was present; now asserts neither, plus Pragma/Expires absence.

Add test_docs_endpoints_are_cache_hardened as a regression guard for the /docs, /redoc, /openapi.json Web Cache Deception fix on this branch.

Signed-off-by: Jonathan Springer <jps@s390x.com>
commits.author: Jonathan Springer

commits.message:
test(security): unit-test docs path classifier instead of request flow

The previous test_docs_endpoints_are_cache_hardened drove a request through the full middleware stack and asserted no-store/private on the response. That assertion always failed because DocsAuthMiddleware is registered AFTER SecurityHeadersMiddleware (mcpgateway/main.py:2927 vs 2886), making it the OUTER wrapper. An unauthenticated GET /docs is short-circuited by DocsAuth with a 401 ORJSONResponse before the response can traverse SecurityHeaders, so no cache headers are attached.

Replace it with a focused unit test that constructs SecurityHeadersMiddleware directly and asserts that /docs, /redoc, and /openapi.json are classified as protected by _is_protected_path(). This validates the same regression guard (the EXEMPTED entries must stay removed) without depending on the full middleware chain.

Signed-off-by: Jonathan Springer <jps@s390x.com>
commits.author: Jonathan Springer
